prompt: A face recognition model trained mostly on light-skinned faces works worse on darker skin.
why: A model learns from the examples it sees, and darker-skinned faces were rare in its training photos. Under-representing a group in the data makes it work worse for that group.
trap: Imbalance is about rare outcomes; this is about people left out.

prompt: A hiring model learned from past hires who were mostly men, and now favors men.
tells: past hires who were mostly men
why: The model copied the pattern in past hiring decisions, including their unfairness to women. Data that records past bias teaches the model that bias.

prompt: A speech model trained on American accents struggles with Scottish speakers.
why: Scottish speakers were missing from the training audio, so the model never learned their speech. Groups left out of the data get worse results.
trap: It's not the model's size; it's who's in the data.

prompt: The loan data reflects old lending practices that excluded some neighborhoods.
why: Old lending practices excluded some neighborhoods, so the data shows them as risky for reasons that weren't fair. A model trained on it repeats that history.

prompt: An image generator draws mostly men for 'CEO' because the training photos did.
why: The training photos showed mostly men as CEOs, so the generator learned that link. Bias in the training data shows up in the outputs.
trap: It is generative, but the problem described is the data.

prompt: Before training, the team checks whether every group of users is fairly represented.
tells: every group of users is fairly represented
why: Checking that every group of users appears fairly before training is how you catch biased data early, before the model learns from it.
trap: Groups of people, not rare outcomes.
